name: GIMM-VFI
plain: GIMM-VFI (GIMM-VFI-R and its perceptual GIMM-VFI-R-P, Guo et al., NeurIPS 2024): makes the frame at any time between two video frames from a learned continuous motion field (RAFT flow), for slow motion and higher frame rates. Non-commercial code and weights (S-Lab License 1.0).
summary: GIMM-VFI (Guo et al., NeurIPS 2024), the RAFT-based GIMM-VFI-R: arbitrary-time video frame interpolation. RAFT estimates the flow between both frames in both directions; a generalizable implicit motion model (a SIREN MLP on time and position, conditioned on the forward-splatted flow latents) predicts the flow at the requested time; an AMT-style decoder refines it with the bidirectional feature correlation and blends both warped frames. Any time in [0, 1]. `gimm-vfi-r` is trained for accuracy, `gimm-vfi-r-p` adds an LPIPS loss for sharper, perceptually better frames.

papers.title: Generalizable Implicit Motion Modeling for Video Frame Interpolation

limitations: At 480 x 854 the standalone GIMM-VFI-R FP32 TensorRT engine returned different frames from portable FP32. Mean normalized absolute pixel error was 0.07687. The same ONNX file run in ONNX Runtime measured 0.000029.

At 480 x 854 the FP32 GIMM-VFI-R-P TensorRT encoders took 1190 ms versus 1231 ms for paired portable FP32. Estimated peak allocated memory was 3592 MiB versus 3282 MiB. The speed table also includes the faster FP16 modes.

The GIMM-VFI-R feature encoder alone passed the 16-triplet check. End-to-end FP32 latency was 1210 ms versus 1230 ms for paired portable FP32, with a PSNR change of at most 0.0395 dB on the checked triplets.
task_io: Input: two RGB images (consecutive frames). Output: the frame between them at `timestep` (0.5 by default; 0 = the first, 1 = the second), RGB in [0, 1].
